hints: Look at the width of each number-of-readings curve and where its centre or peak sits relative to the mark $V$ on the volume axis.
Recall that precise means repeatable with small spread so a narrow peak, while accurate means the mean is close to the true value $V$.
Compare X which is broad but centred on $V$, Y which is very narrow but centred below $V$, and Z which peaks at $V$ but has a long tail to large volume.
walkthrough: Note the given information: true volume is $V$, and each graph plots number of readings against measured volume for equipment X, Y and Z.
State the rules: a precise set has small random spread so a narrow distribution, and an accurate set has a mean value close to the true value $V$.
Check X: the curve is broad and symmetric about $V$, so spread is large but mean is at $V$ - accurate but not precise.
Check Y: the curve is very tall and narrow but its peak is well below $V$, so spread is small but mean is below $V$ - precise but not accurate.
Check Z: the curve peaks near $V$ but has a long tail to volumes much larger than $V$, so it is neither narrow overall nor has a mean at $V$ - neither precise nor accurate.
Count the results: 1 precise piece (Y) and 1 accurate piece (X). This is option A.

A.explanation: Only Y is precise with its narrow tall peak, and only X is accurate with its distribution centred on $V$.

B.explanation: Z is not accurate because its long tail to high volume shifts its mean above $V$ even though its peak is at $V$.

C.explanation: X is not precise because its curve is broad, and Z is not precise because of its wide tail to the right.

D.explanation: Only one distribution is narrow and only one is centred on $V$, so 2 and 2 overcounts both qualities.
